final_text: "Now is my chance to slip away," I thought. But the tones that then filled the air stopped me. Mrs. Fairfax had said Mr. Rochester possessed a fine voice, and he did—a mellow, powerful bass into which he poured his own feeling and force, finding a path through the ear to the heart and there waking sensation strangely. I waited until the last full, resonant vibration had died away—until the tide of talk, briefly checked, had resumed its flow. Then I left my sheltered corner and made my exit by the side door, which was fortunately close. From there a narrow passage led to the hall. Crossing it, I noticed my shoe was loose; I stopped to tie it, kneeling on the mat at the foot of the staircase. I heard the dining room door open; a gentleman came out. Rising quickly, I stood face to face with him: it was Mr. Rochester.
